notes: GeoTalk 1.6: two independent attacks on the internet-call problem. First, a second, fully independent live-voice engine now sits between WebRTC and Push-to-Talk: when the WebRTC engine cannot start or cannot connect on a phone, the call attempts direct phone-to-phone UDP voice instead (shown in the call screen as 'Live • Direct UDP'), and only drops to Push-to-Talk bursts when both phones have not confirmed real live voice within a few seconds — so calls can go fully live, both ways at once, even on phones where WebRTC cannot start. Second, the problem report can now capture native crash details: if the app is ever stopped by a low-level system fault, the exact signal, fault address and program location are recorded and included in the next problem report, so the real cause can be found and fixed faster. Everything from 1.5 is kept: the call safety guard resets properly on every new version so WebRTC always gets a genuinely fresh attempt on each update, standard WebRTC connection settings, call signaling on its own dedicated thread so the calling engine is never blocked by network writes, the engine connects first and attaches your voice only after the connection is up, proper telephony audio mode with audio focus, the update popup no longer appears after you have already updated, incoming calls ring with your default ringtone and vibration, problem reports always record the newest incident, near-instant call setup, direct phone-to-phone WebRTC voice first, Cloudflare TURN relay (UDP, TCP and TLS 443) when a network blocks the direct path, Push-to-Talk as the final fallback, plus internet and Bluetooth chat + voice calls, voice messages and in-app updates.
